what_its_for: Levocarnitine is used to treat or prevent low levels of carnitine in your body. Carnitine is a natural substance that helps your body turn fat into energy. You may need this medicine if your body cannot make enough carnitine on its own, if you have certain inherited conditions that affect how your body uses carnitine, or if you are on kidney dialysis which can remove carnitine from your blood.
how_to_take: Levocarnitine comes as a liquid solution or tablets taken by mouth, or as an injection given by a healthcare provider. Take the liquid or tablets with food or shortly after eating to help prevent stomach upset. If you are using the liquid form, measure your dose carefully using the measuring device provided with your medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. Space your doses evenly throughout the day, such as with breakfast, lunch, and dinner, unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
dosing: The dose your doctor prescribes will depend on your age, weight, and the condition being treated. For adults, a typical oral dose is 990 mg (one tablet or 10 mL of liquid) taken two to three times daily with meals. For children, the dose is usually based on body weight and is determined by your doctor. For patients on dialysis, the dose is usually given as an injection by your healthcare team after each dialysis session. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store levocarnitine tablets and oral liquid at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the liquid in its original container and keep it tightly closed. Protect from light and excessive heat. Do not freeze the liquid. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol while taking levocarnitine, as it may affect how well the medicine works. Do not take D-carnitine or DL-carnitine supplements (sometimes sold in health food stores as 'carnitine') while using levocarnitine — these forms can actually block levocarnitine from working in your body. Tell your doctor about all vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you take, as some may interact with levocarnitine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience any of the following: seizures (even if you have never had one before), chest pain or irregular heartbeat, severe muscle weakness, signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you notice a strong fishy body odor (this can be a side effect), persistent nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, or diarrhea that does not go away, or if you feel that your condition is not improving.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some improvement within a few weeks of starting levocarnitine, but it may take several months to see the full benefit, especially if you have a long-term carnitine deficiency. Your doctor will check your carnitine blood levels periodically to make sure the medicine is working properly. Keep taking levocarnitine even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Levocarnitine is naturally present in breast milk, but talk to your doctor before using it while nursing. Children: Levocarnitine can be used in children; the dose will be carefully calculated based on your child's weight. Elderly patients: Older adults can generally use levocarnitine safely, but your doctor may monitor you more closely. Kidney disease and dialysis patients: If you are on dialysis, your dose will typically be given as an injection after each session — follow your dialysis team's instructions carefully.
